strategy.summary: Normteile Brucker KG is a sound family-owned C-parts maker (60 staff, equity ratio 36 %, stable credit index, audit A). To it we are a small customer, about 0.3 % of its turnover. It supplies the stud bolt 360013 as our single source and the washer 360030 split 50/50 with Leitner. Head office has frozen price reductions until December 2027, and price changes above 2 % need its pricing committee. Its stated exception is a multi-year volume agreement, and it openly invites talks on payment and call-off terms. No should-cost exists, so evidence on margin is thin. Stud bolt drivers rose (alloy 1.4301 and the fastener PPI), even though its price fell steadily in past renewals. On the washer, Brucker is already cheaper than Leitner but has clearly worse quality and delivery. Expect one move only, priced through terms: a 24-month volume commitment plus on-time or faster payment. Defend against an alloy-driven increase on the stud bolt, and use washer quality for a ppm commitment rather than price.
strategy.decision_maker: Key account manager handles day-to-day (can decide price changes up to 2 %); sales director sets stance; pricing committee (meets every two weeks) approves changes above 2 %; head office issued the price freeze.

persona.style: process-driven, rule-bound (uniform price list, committee approval), cooperative on logistics and payment
other_traits: prefers multi-year volume deals over discounts

needs.detail: Its only stated route to a price change is a multi-year volume agreement; rising forecasts are already shared with it.
It invites talks on payment conditions; we pay most invoices a few days late. It wants on-time or faster payment as convenience, not out of distress.
Wants its uniform list price kept for all customers through the freeze period.
Logistics and call-off efficiency (returnable boxes, call-off flexibility).

Price changes above 2 % need the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.
Prices are fixed per calendar year and changes need notice before year end. The framework renews automatically unless terminated.
The stud bolt has no other approved source, which limits our exit.

Rising, shared bolt forecast gives substance to a binding multi-year volume offer.
Rising washer volume, possibly with a quota shift, is worth more to it.
The sales director was open on payment and call-off flexibility, so trades there are legitimate.
The washer complaints support asking for a ppm commitment and keeping the chargeback.
A second source with better quality makes a quota shift on the washer credible without citing its price.
The recent alloy fall counters an alloy-based increase on the stud bolt.

trades.why: A multi-year agreement is its stated condition for any price move; 24 months captures the value.
Binding volume within our forecast need is the core of a volume agreement.
It invites payment talks; faster or reliably on-time payment is cheap for us to give in exchange for price.
Washer quality is poor; it can repair its standing at low cost to itself.
A fixed price during its freeze protects us from the alloy rise on the stud bolt.

price_view.reasoning: The freeze, the approval ladder and its uniform list leave little room. Bolt drivers rose, and the bolt price already fell over past renewals. The washer is already below the rival price. Realistic outcome: hold the price, or a small cut within the key account manager's own mandate, bought with length, volume and payment. There is no should-cost to test margin.

Lead with concrete binding volume and length in round 1
Commit to on-time payment and address our late payments proactively
Raise washer quality factually, with records, and ask for a fix commitment
dont: Do not demand a plain discount on standard items

strategy.writer_notes: On the stud bolt, defend the current price against an alloy argument with the recent alloy fall and the contract's notice rule. On the washer, push quality and delivery rather than price; a quota shift toward Leitner is a quiet option, but never cite Leitner's price. Close quickly after the first hold.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for either part, so the margin over full cost cannot be measured; the room on price can only be judged from index movement, price history and rival prices. The evidence is thin here.

Stud bolt 360013: the weighted drivers rose over 12 months. Fasteners PPI +1.7% x 0.32, alloy surcharge 1.4301 +8.6% x 0.28 and labour +2.7% x 0.10 add up to about +3.2% on the price. Yet the price fell 12.4% since 2023 (33.35 to 29.23 per 100). The supplier could argue for an increase, but contract §3.1 fixes the 2026 price. Any 2027 change needed 90 days' notice before year end, and none is recorded; its quote of 2026-09-04 holds 29.23.

The 1.4301 surcharge is volatile. It is -7.6% since 2026-06 and -17.6% below its 36-month peak. The fall since June is the only checkable for-us counter to an alloy-based increase; the peak comparison is context only.

Washer 360030: price flat at 12.64 per 1000 since 2023. Drivers add only about +1.3% (PPI +1.7% x 0.64, LCI +2.7% x 0.08). Brucker is already 1.1% below second source Leitner (12.78) and was below Leitner in the 2025 RFQ (12.80 vs 13.06). There is little room for a cut and little case for a rise; rival figures favour Brucker, so we should not cite them.

Brucker repeatedly states a price freeze on reductions until Dec 2027 and says only multi-year volume agreements change prices. It is open on payment terms and call-off flexibility, and changes above 2% need its pricing committee. Realistic price room is roughly 0 to -2%, and only in trade for commitment or volume (+11% / +9% forecast).

supplier_wants: Hold current list prices (no discounts until Dec 2027)
On-time payment (we pay late 89.5% of the time) / possibly faster payment
Possibly pass through the 1.4301 alloy rise on 360013 for 2027
risks: The 360013 drivers (+~3.2%) support an increase claim, and Brucker is our single source with its own tooling.
Citing the rival price or quote on 360030 shows Brucker is cheapest and weakens us.
Our late payment record invites a counter-demand.
We are 0.3% of its turnover and it is financially sound, so pushing hard risks it walking away.

Anchors any 2027 discussion at 29.23.
Anchors the washer at 12.64.

findings.text: Price is formally frozen by head office: the 2027 price list applies to all customers without exception until December 2027. The sales director confirmed that all price reductions are frozen and offered payment terms and call-off flexibility instead. The sales rep has no mandate on list price, so asking for a straight price cut will hit a wall.

There is an approval ladder. Price changes above 2 % need the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. Any move above 2 % adds at least a two-week delay. Below 2 % the key account manager can likely decide alone.

The stated exception to the freeze is a multi-year volume agreement: standard items are not discounted, but multi-year volume deals change prices. This is the door for a longer contract with binding volume. Forecast volumes are up about 11 % (360013) and 9 % (360030), and these forecasts have already been shared with the supplier.

The freeze has not stopped deals in the past. On 360013 the price fell 12.4 % since 2023, and renewals settled below the supplier's own ask. On 360030 the price has been flat at 12.64 for three years. The freeze is new (2026) and may soften if we bring a volume or term trade.

They are a healthy, small family KG: 60 staff, EUR 29.1 M turnover, 36 % equity, stable credit index 185, VDA 6.3 audit A. There is no financial stress, and we are only about 0.3 % of their turnover, so they can afford to walk away. What they want is cash and logistics efficiency, not survival.

Payment behaviour is a sensitivity. We pay 89.5 % of invoices late, about 4 days on average, maximum 13 days. They explicitly invite talks on payment conditions. Paying on time, or earlier against a price concession, is a cheap trade for us.

Their style is process-driven and cooperative on logistics: they introduced returnable boxes on their own initiative. The news item (apprentice award) is noise. Overall the evidence on their decision makers is thin: we know only of a sales director, a key account manager, head office and the pricing committee.

Keeping the uniform price list intact for all customers
risks: A price cut above 2 % triggers the pricing committee and a delay of two weeks or more
Pushing against the head-office freeze may make them walk away; they are sound and we are a small customer
Single source with supplier-owned tooling on 360013 weakens our exit
Our late payments give them a complaint to raise
Alloy surcharge 1.4301 up 8.6 % gives them an argument for an increase on 360013

findings.text: Framework agreement runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and covers both parts (stud bolt 360013, washer 360030). Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, so by about 2026-10-02 for 2027 prices. Payment is 30 days net, against our 60-day standard. Delivery is DAP with a 7-day lead time. The quality clause sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint. The contract renews automatically for 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice, i.e. by 2027-04-01.

History shows the supplier settles about 2 pp below its ask in every renewal. On the stud bolt it opened with cuts (-5.1, -1.1, -0.7) and settled deeper (-6.3, -2.8, -3.8); the price fell 12.4% since 2023. On the washer it asked for increases (+1.7, +3.5, +1.2) and settled at 0 each time; the price has been flat at 12.64 per 1000.

The latest signals suggest the pattern of cuts may stop. In 2026 the supplier stated that its price list is frozen for all customers until December 2027 and that only multi-year volume agreements change prices. It is open on payment terms, logistics and call-off flexibility. Price changes above 2% need approval from its pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.

Dependency differs by part. The stud bolt is single-sourced with this supplier at 100% quota since 2015. The washer is split 50/50 with sup:70610 Leitner. In the 2025 benchmark RFQ the washer was awarded to Leitner at EUR 13.06 per 1000, and we now pay Leitner 12.78, so this supplier is the cheaper washer source. The library says the supplier owns the tooling, but the master data says tooling_owner n/a; for standard parts this barrier is weak.
We matter little to this supplier: about EUR 81k spend, roughly 0.3% of its turnover, and the spend is falling. It is financially sound (credit index 185 unchanged, VDA 6.3 grade A).

findings.text: Delivery is steady but below target: OTD 88.0% vs requested (90.0% vs confirmed) in the rolling 12 months to 2026-09, down from 89.6% a year earlier, against a 95% contract target. It is still above the peer median of 84.6%, so this is a mild lever, not a strong one. Late lines run 17 days late on average (max 27).

Quality is deteriorating. Rolling ppm rose from 125 (2025Q1) to 293 (2026Q2) and stands at 257 now, against 182 a year earlier. QN count went from 12 to 19. It is still well below the peer median of 457 ppm, and 8D discipline is clean (0 overdue), so it can argue its case.

The washer part:360030 is the problem part. Its 12-month ppm is 334 against 59 for the dual source sup:70610, on the same volume. There were 12 supplier-caused QNs in the last 12 months, recurring porosity and coating defects, and EUR 1,200 recharged. On-time delivery for this part is 84% (late lines up to 27 days late). The washer price is also flat at 12.64 since 2023, slightly below sup:70610's 12.78.

The stud bolt part:360013 performs better: 92% OTD, 164 ppm, 7 QNs in the last 12 months. The latest QN, qn:20005021 (wrong material certificate), has no closed 8D yet. Its price has fallen 12.4% since 2023, to 29.23 per 100. It is single source and the supplier owns the tooling.

Recharging the EUR 150 flat fee is inconsistent: many supplier-caused QNs show EUR 0 recharged. Our real defect cost is understated, and we have room to enforce the fee or ask for a chargeback/ppm commitment.

The volume outlook is up, and the forecasts are shared with the supplier: 291k vs 261k ordered for part:360013 (+11.5%), and 736k vs 677k for part:360030 (+8.7%). The supplier said only multi-year volume agreements move its prices. Volume plus a longer term is our trade currency, though it is small for the supplier (spend about 0.3% of its turnover).

call-off flexibility discussion instead of price moves
risks: Its quality is better than peers (257 vs 457 ppm), so hard quality claims can backfire.

arguments.text: Stud bolt 360013 has fallen every year while its cost drivers rose: price 33.35 to 29.23 per 100 (-12.4 % since 2023, cuts of -6.3 %, -2.8 % and -3.8 %). Meanwhile the 1.4301 alloy surcharge is +8.6 % over 12 months and the fastener PPI is +1.7 %. Further reductions are not justified. If anything, an alloy-driven adjustment would be.
Our list price applies to all customers without exception until December 2027, and head office has frozen reductions. This is a company-wide policy, not a position aimed at Hollerau.
On the washer we are already cheaper than Leitner (12.64 vs 12.78 per 1000). Our price has been held flat for four years despite labour costs rising +2.7 % and steel +7.3 % since January.
The contract fixes prices per calendar year and runs to 2027-06-30. Changes need 90 days' notice before year end.
We are a reliable, solid partner. Audit grade A, scorecard class A/green throughout, no overdue 8D reports. We switched to returnable boxes to save the customer handling.
Hollerau pays about 4 days late on average and on 89.5 % of invoices. Better payment discipline is the first thing we would value.

weak_points: Washer quality is poor: 334 ppm versus Leitner's 59 ppm, and complaints are rising (2026Q2 at 293 ppm overall versus 125 in 2025Q1).
On-time delivery is about 88 %, below the contractual 95 % target. The washer is at 84 %, with lateness of up to 27 days.
In the 2025 washer benchmark RFQ we quoted 12.8, below Leitner's 13.06, but lost. That signals they value something besides price and can shift our 50 % share.
Our cost is a basket: power prices are -43 % on 2022, and the fastener PPI is still below its 2023 peak. The alloy surcharge is -17.6 % from its 36-month peak and -44.9 % from its all-time high.
Our key account manager can move prices up to 2 % without committee approval, so the freeze is not absolute.
We said ourselves that multi-year volume agreements do change prices.
Forecasts are rising (bolt 291k, washer 736k), so the customer knows its volume is growing.
No should-cost exists, but the 12.4 % cumulative bolt cuts show we had margin.
wants: A 24-month (or longer) volume commitment on both parts, ideally the extension to 2028.
A larger washer share (e.g. 60-70 %) for us.
Payment on time or faster (e.g. 14 days) in exchange for a small concession.
Call-off schedules and bundled orders, with fewer rush lines.
No index clause that only works downward; any index must be symmetric.
Keep DAP and the returnable boxes.
red_lines: No price cut above 2 % (beyond that the pricing committee will refuse during the freeze).
No customer-specific discount that breaks our uniform list without a multi-year volume trade.
No bolt price cut without volume or term in return.
No ppm commitment with heavy chargebacks beyond the 150 EUR flat fee without time to improve.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the long partnership and point to the four annual bolt reductions totalling -12.4 % while alloy rose +8.6 %. Confirm the 2027 list price holds (bolt 29.23/100, washer 12.64/1000, already below Leitner). Then state that price is not the lever this year, but propose a 24-month volume agreement with on-time payment and planned call-offs, in which we could look at a small step within our own mandate. Acknowledge the washer quality concerns and offer a corrective plan, without opening with a ppm penalty.

rebuttals.answer: We acknowledge the past reductions on the stud bolt and that some drivers rose over the year. Weighted by their share of the part, though, the increases account for only a modest effect on the total price. The alloy surcharge has also fallen markedly in recent months. Our contract fixes the price per calendar year, so we see no basis for an adjustment. We would rather keep today's price stable and secure it with a longer volume commitment.

We respect that this is a company-wide policy and are not asking for an exception from your list. Your own team has told us that multi-year volume agreements do change prices, and that payment and call-off terms are open for discussion. We would like to work within exactly that framework.

We value the stable washer price. For us, though, total cost counts as well as the unit price. Complaints and late deliveries on this part add costs that outweigh small price differences. The price has also not moved in past renewals, which shows the market supports it as it stands. Our washer volume is rising, and that is worth more to you than a price step.

Agreed. The contract fixes prices per calendar year and requires notice for changes, and we intend to honour it on both sides. The term also renews only if neither side gives notice. That makes now the right moment to agree a multi-year package that suits both of us.

The scorecard also shows on-time delivery below the agreed target and complaint levels that have risen over the past year, particularly on the washer. We would like to agree concrete improvements as part of the package.

That is a fair point, and we take it seriously. Our delays have mostly been short, but we are ready to commit to reliable on-time payment, or even faster payment, as part of a multi-year agreement. We would expect that to be reflected in the terms.

press: Your team told us that multi-year volume agreements can change prices; we would like to offer exactly such an agreement.
Our shared forecasts show rising volumes on both parts, and we are prepared to make part of that volume binding over a longer term.
On-time delivery has stayed below the agreed target, especially on the washer, and we would welcome a concrete improvement plan.
Washer complaints have increased over the past year, and we would like to agree a ppm commitment together with corrective actions on porosity and coatings.
As we understand it, your key account manager can agree smaller adjustments without committee approval, which would keep things simple for both of us.
